name: Entiat Ice Fall

approach_variants.name: Phelps Creek and Leroy Basin to a bivy at Icy Lake, then the notch onto the Entiat Glacier
approach_variants.notes: Approach as for the North Face: Phelps Creek trailhead, the Phelps Creek trail to the Leroy Creek crossing, then the unmarked climbers' trail up the north side of Leroy Creek into the basin, and on up toward Ice Lakes. Sources spell it Icy Lake as often as Ice Lakes; it is the same water. Parties bivy on ledges above the south side of the lake, below the South Ridge. That is the sensible camp because the South Ridge is the descent — but be clear that it puts you on the wrong side of the mountain for this route, so the morning starts with a long traverse over a cliff band to reach the access notch. One party set themselves a turnaround rule of two hours from camp to the notch, on the grounds that any slower and there would not be time to finish. Cross the talus above the lake to the notch that lets you onto the Entiat Glacier. Rope up and descend to find a short crossing through the ablation zone of the receding glacier — this is harder than the old published photograph suggests. Skirt below the rock spur and head up toward the icefall.
approach_variants.season: Late summer for the ice, roughly Jul-Aug; the icefall has receded a long way and how much of it is climbable varies year to year
hazards: A decoy notch at about 6,900 ft that leads to a long scree detour
Crossing the ablation zone of a receding glacier, trickier than published photographs show
Big crevasses with vertical steps in the icefall
Crumbly rock with scarce protection on the nine hundred feet above the ice
A long traverse over a cliff band from the Icy Lake camp before the route even starts
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The notch is the thing you can get wrong, and there is a documented decoy. The access notch is at about 7,200 ft. A climbers' path leads to a different notch at about 6,900 ft, and a party who took it for the right one paid for the error with a long detour in the wrong direction up an ugly scree bash. If the notch you have reached is around six-nine rather than seven-two, keep going.

Once through the correct notch and onto the glacier, the sequence is: descend, cross the ablation zone, pass under the rock spur, then work rightward beneath the headwall. Arrival at the climbing is a change in the ice — you move from walking to big crevasses with short vertical steps, and above those the angle relaxes to about thirty-five degrees of ice running up to the base of the rock.

That base of rock is the second, unmistakable transition: roughly nine hundred feet of fourth and low fifth class above it, with several ramps to choose between. Take the line of least resistance trending slightly toward the ridge crest. The rock is crumbly and protection is scarce, so running belays are the usual method rather than pitching it. There is a distinctive step-across at the top of a couloir partway up.

A note on how much ice you will actually find: in a heavy snow year one party bypassed roughly two pitches of the icefall on steep snow slopes off to the side, and the whole icefall took them an hour of running belays where they had budgeted six. Do not plan the day around a pitch count from an older description.

Descent is the South Ridge, which took that party half an hour — which is exactly why the camp is where it is.

approach: Same trailhead and lower approach as the North Face: Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft) via FR 6211, up the Phelps Creek Trail to the Leroy Creek crossing, then the climber's trail into Leroy Creek Basin (~6,100-6,200 ft, ~5 miles). From camp, continue toward the Seven Fingered Jack-Maude col/Icy Lake area and descend to the Entiat Glacier to reach the icefall.
itinerary: Day 1: Approach ~4,000 ft of gain over several hours from the trailhead to a bivy site above Icy Lake. Day 2: Descend to and cross the Entiat Glacier, climb the icefall (running belay through ice steps) then ~900 ft of 4th/low-5th class rock to the summit, descend the South Ridge back toward camp. Day 3: Hike out.
beta: From a bivy above Icy Lake in the Leroy Creek Basin area, descend to the Entiat Glacier surface, cross the ablation zone, and climb the icefall's short vertical ice steps and ramps between crevasses (running belay) before turning right onto ~900 vertical feet of crumbly 4th/low-5th class rock leading to the summit. The glacier has receded substantially since Fred Beckey's era, when the route reportedly had 9 pitches of ice; today's icefall is shorter and more variable year to year.

pitch_detail.notes: From the notch above Icy Lake, rope up and descend onto the Entiat Glacier, then find a short way across the ablation zone of the shrinking glacier. The crossing is trickier than older photos suggest. Skirt below the rock spur and head up toward the icefall.

Work rightward beneath the headwall through big crevasses, climbing short vertical ice steps and ramps between them; most parties move on a running belay with screws and a picket. In a big snow year steep snow slopes to one side can bypass part of the ice. The icefall has shrunk greatly and its shape changes from year to year.

Above the crevasses, gentler slopes of ice and snow at around 35° lead to the base of the rock. The rock above is slower than it looks from here; allow several hours for it rather than a quick scramble.

Turn right off the ice onto the rock, where several ramps offer a start. The rock is crumbly and protection is scarce, so running belays are the usual method. Take the line of least resistance, trending slightly toward the ridge crest.

Continue on loose fourth and low-fifth-class ground toward the crest; the rock section totals roughly 900 vertical feet and commonly takes several hours. Near the top there is a step-across at the head of a couloir. Test holds before weighting them; rockfall onto the party below is the main hazard.
A short walk leads to the heavily cairned 9,082 ft summit. Descend the South Ridge on foot, which is quick in good conditions and returns toward the Icy Lake bivy ledges.

waypoints.name: Phelps Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-2 at Coles Corner, about 20 miles east of Stevens Pass, turn north on SR 207. Just past the bridge over the Wenatchee River turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto the Chiwawa River Road, FR 62, and follow it more than 20 miles as it turns to rough gravel. Turn right onto Phelps Creek Road, FR 6211, and drive about 2 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,500 ft. Fill out a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Mount Maude Summit
waypoints.directions: Hike the Phelps Creek Trail about 3.5 miles to Leroy Creek, climb the climbers' trail on its north side into Leroy Basin, and continue to a bivy on ledges above the south side of Ice Lake. Traverse talus to the access notch at about 7,200 ft (not the decoy notch near 6,900 ft), rope up and descend onto the Entiat Glacier, cross its ablation zone below the rock spur, and climb the icefall and about 900 ft of fourth- and low-fifth-class rock to the summit.
